column1: # Is there anything in Bitwuzla's own settings worth having on this corpus?
# Every STP number in RESULTS.md comes from a configuration picked by measuring
# it -- SAT backend, when incrementality engages, whether that adapts, and the
# CNF-effort threshold. Bitwuzla's come from no options at all. That makes the
# published comparison "tuned STP against Bitwuzla as KLEE ships it", which is
# a fair description of what a KLEE user gets and is not the same claim as one
# solver being faster than the other.
# Two things are asked here.
# bwz-noabs moves the one knob KLEE already wires. The corpus is floating-point
# heavy and the abstraction targets bvmul, bvudiv and bvurem -- where fp.mul
# and fp.div land once blasted, and where STP was found weakest -- so it is the
# setting most likely to matter, in either direction.
# bwz-incr closes the larger, structural gap. KLEE holds one STP session and
# pushes and pops around each query; BitwuzlaSolverImpl called bitwuzla_new and
# bitwuzla_delete inside the per-query path, so every query met a cold solver
# and every learned clause was discarded. --bitwuzla-incremental keeps one
# session, which is the same courtesy STP has had throughout.
# stp-thr0 rides along as the reference the rest are quoted against.
# label <TAB> backend <TAB> LD_LIBRARY_PATH for libstp (or -) <TAB> extra klee args
bwz-default
bwz-noabs
bwz-incr
stp-thr0
